sacks_made.label: sacks made
sacks_made.why: the feed attributes 1.3 sacks made per team-game against roughly 2 in real football, so this column is declared degraded league-wide rather than scored as if the events did not happen

fumbles_lost.label: fumbles lost
fumbles_lost.why: the feed attributes 0.16 fumbles lost per team-game against roughly 0.6 in real football, so this column is declared missing league-wide rather than scored as if the events did not happen

fumbles_forced.label: forced fumbles
fumbles_forced.why: the feed attributes 0.08 forced fumbles per team-game against roughly 0.6 in real football, so this column is declared missing league-wide rather than scored as if the events did not happen

column_gate_basis: a column is USABLE where the league-wide per-team-game rate reaches 70% of what a season of FBS football produces, DEGRADED between 30% and 70%, and MISSING below that. A DEGRADED or MISSING column is never published as a rate: a team with no rows in it has an unmeasured column, not a perfect one.
garbage_time_basis: a play is garbage time when the margin exceeds 38 in the second quarter, 28 in the third or 22 in the fourth, measured on the running score the feed carries. It is a clock-and-score rule, not a win-probability model, and it is stated so a reader can disagree with it.
limits: no expected-points or EPA measure appears here: the feed carries no next-score information, so none is computable and none is invented
pressures short of a sack, snap counts, blocking and coverage are not in this feed at any price
a play whose yardage the feed does not attribute is excluded from the third-down denominator rather than scored as a stop
overtime plays are counted and reported separately; they are not folded into a per-drive rate
note: Every rate here is a count from this season’s plays and is NOT opponent-adjusted. A team that has played weaker opponents reads better than it is, and the packet that uses these says so beside every pairing.
